note: Chosen for PARSER coverage, not for chemistry. Each entry says which line shapes it is here to produce, so a future edit can tell a deliberate case from a decorative one. See README.md.

molecules.name: aspirin
molecules.why: the project's default probe molecule; exercises the widest set of descriptor, topology and medicinal-chemistry lines

molecules.name: benzene
molecules.why: the smallest pi system, so Huckel emits a POSITIVE HOMO and a signed orbital-energy list -- the two shapes the sign bug hid behind

molecules.name: naphthalene
molecules.why: a longer orbital-energy list (10 entries), which is what makes the value-LIST case visibly different from a scalar

molecules.name: pyridine
molecules.why: a heteroaromatic, so Huckel adds its heteroatom caveat -- a prose line that must stay unsplit

molecules.name: water
molecules.why: two elements only, so elemental analysis emits the attached-unit form ('O: 88.81%') at its shortest

molecules.name: ammonia
molecules.why: a small polar molecule with a non-zero dipole along an axis, exercising signed components

molecules.name: chloromethane
molecules.why: a TWO-LETTER element symbol in elemental analysis ('Cl: 70.22%'), and the dipole case the sign bug was reported on

molecules.name: acetic_acid
molecules.why: an ionizable centre, so the pKa and logD lines appear -- the ones written with '=' and with no separator at all

molecules.name: caffeine
molecules.why: fused heteroaromatic with several rings; the richest single source of lines in this set

molecules.name: glycine_zwitterion
molecules.why: a formally charged species, so the dipole reports its origin-dependence caveat and charge lines carry explicit signs
